When it was delivered, they left it against the front door as I was not home and I knew the delivery people would probably not want to haul this back to their truck. The box was really abused and shredding apart. After unscrewing the first protective cardboard piece from the bottom of the bike, a nut came off. Little did I know that it was needed to hold the crossbar on the floor. So I figured a way to hold the nut in place while screwing in the screw that holds the bar. Finally when the bike was completely assembled, the wheel would not turn! Then I tried going backwards and that freed something up for a little bit. Then I go foward and it goes a little bit and locks up.
Plus it made a lot of rattling noises like something was loose inside. Anyway, Stamina sent the replacement part. ...so again, the first thing you do is unscrew the protective cardboard for the bottom and the nut falls off again! Now that the bike is all put together again,
my complaint now is that I am too short to sit comfortably on the seat. It is not made for a person that is 5'2".

I did call the company for them to look into the "nut" problem.

3) I used an Inspire Charger Dock which I'm very glad I purchased after reading reviews. It has a long USB cable, magnetically clicks to the Inspire and makes charging very easy.
4) The watch was at 92% after the required firmware update via the Fitbit app.
5) Today, after less than 24% the watch is already at 82%. There were a lot of reviews about how quickly the Inspire loses battery charge. I have 'all day sync' and 'always connected' turned off and only synced with the app three times today, but it still lost 10% of the charge.
6) I had some problems connecting the Inspire to the Fitbit app. I tried about 6 times before the app connected. I kept getting a Fitbit maintenance error. The app then took about an hour to update the firmware on the Inspire. I did have to reboot my phone before the Inspire successfully paired with the app.
7) Since pairing the Inspire quickly synced each time I opened the app.

I'll update my review after trying out out for a few weeks.

NOTE: The Inspire can be returned to Amazon within 45 days and has a limited 1 year warranty with support via Fitbit customer service (2 year warranty if purchased in the EEU). You will receive an offer in the app to extend the warranty to 2 years. I didn't personally feel like spending an additional 24.99 for an extended warranty. text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker Well.  I have been using this for many months.  I waited to be provide a fair and honest assessment. This is a review of my personal experience.  My main disappointment is the syncing with the fitbit app - I have a samsung android smart phone with the app installed, further - the app is current with all provided updates. The fitbit 3 itself needs to be "restarted" multiple times a week- you must attach it to the charging cable, push/hold the side button and hold for up to 10 seconds to force restart.  Otherwise it does NOT sync.  SUPER annoying.  And then there are the times when it randomly decides NOT to record my sleep record.  GRRRR....  I have had multiple fitbits - beginning with their gen one version.  Provides reasonably accurate info - BUT if you must FIGHT to get the info through sync - it sort of looses it appeal.  While it says that it does allow you to swim, so water friendly, I do not soak or submerge the fitbit.  I don't remove it as I wash dishes or my hands - so it has been splashed with water.  When I get in the pool, I take it off.  I just don't trust the water friendly part.  I may go back to my fitbit 2 because it is so much more slim and attractive.  These are somewhat clunky.  I also have tried the much larger watch face version - I quickly stopped using it as it is horribly uncomfortable in size alone - the fitbit 3 is much better than that watch face/square version.  The bands on the fitbit 3 are easy to change.  I have not placed a screen/face protection shields on and haven't had too much trouble with scratching - in fact I don't see any - yet.  So I can't say how easy it is to replace the face - or to place the protection screening on.  I wear my fitbit on one wrist during the day and change it to the other wrist at night while sleeping - I use an alcohol wipe to clean the back of the unit and band several times a week. Further I don't wear it one or two nights a week to give my skin a break and to charge it.  I did purchase the perforated (holes in the band) to provide more breathability.  It is a workable step monitor.  I just wish it would sync more reliably and without forcing a restart which you can't just do where ever you are - but must be done while attached to the charging cord.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and I hope this info was helpful to you in some way.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Scout Internal Frame Backpack – High-Performance Backpack for Hiking, Camping, Backpacking; Adjustable for Men, Women and Youth; Rain Cover; Buck Brown, 65L I wish there were some places at the very bottom of the bag so I could lash a cord or whatever attachment through (to attach a tent, sleeping pad, etc) and not have it bounce around. I'm sure the loops are useful for hiking axes or some such thing, but I'd prefer to have a way to not have something flip-flopping around back there. In other words, I'd like a little more reinforced bottom with some possibilities for such a thing, even if it added up to half a pound. ON THE OTHER HAND: I love the hunter green version. Great for camouflage but also has a great attached bright yellow rain fly that you can cover your entire pack with. This will help in emergencies, even if you had to cut it off for a flag, whatever.

I like the top-loading aspect with the very secure extra-gusseted closure that closes underneath the toggle.. Great feature. What I would have liked, also, is something I have in a Kelty pack I bought once: The top portion of that Kelty bag came loose entirely and you could use it as a shoulder bag or fanny/waist pack. It seems like a waste to not have that feature now as it was so useful.

I really like the separate sleeping bag compartment, though there are some gaps where the zipper doesn't go around completely. If you lose some gear, you may have to remove the sleeping bag or whatever and check to see if it didn't sleep down into that compartment. The pros on that feature are that it's easy to get to that without pulling everything out of the pack, or you have a separate compartment for whatever gear you need to get at more easily. Granted you have to take the pack off, but it's a nice option. I'd recommend using a contractor bag or trash bag, etc, to line the bottom of the top section so gear doesn't fall through into the sleeping bag compartment.

The fabric looks to be of good lasting quality and nicely water resistent, though I haven't field tested this yet. Though I'm not used to the idea of having to have to take the aluminum slats out, having a friend help adjust them to the curve of my back, I can see that this can be a great feature. My gripe on that is that, though it'll be a great option, the labels give no directions on how to line those things up to your back when you bend them. Not interested in spending a lot of time experimenting with that once the pack's loaded and I find that it's just not the right fit (yet).

Overall, I give this 5 stars. The price is wonderful and for a person my size (5'6"), it holds the optimal amount of liters/inches of gear and will be versatile enough to play with. I like that there is a hook, that is also like a clip so I can clip it to a bag if necessary. I also really like that there is a lid for the the mouthpiece to keep it protected. It's been dropped a couple of times with no issues. I have only hand washed it, and so far no issues (only been a couple of weeks). It's cute, easy to carry, but when left in the car, it spits at me when I re-open it! A couple of other people have mentioned it on reviews as well. It's not worth me returning for that reason alone, but I would probably look elsewhere next time since there are so many other options.
Update - I've now had this a couple of months and traveled with it on an airplane. My old water bottles would occasionally "spit" from the pressure change on the plane, so I was fully ready (with my sleeve over the spout) to catch the water from this bottle. Oh, wow...it was like Niagara Falls! The funniest part was that the water ended up in my lap, so it looked like I just didn't make it to the rest room in time. I thought it was hilarious, but I can see how some would not. On the flight back, I just unscrewed the lid a tiny bit to release the pressure and no issues. The hook came in super handy when I wanted to clip it to the outside of my backpack.
The real reason I am updating my review is because it was hard to drink out of the straw due to the suction. As dumb as this sounds, I found myself drinking water less because of this issue. I went back and read some additional reviews and a couple people mentioned removing the little piece in the cap that effects the airflow. Eureka! It now works perfectly! I'll be using this bottle more often now.

Valeo Padded Ocelot Lifting Gloves, Gym Gloves, Workout Gloves, Exercise Gloves for Powerlifting, Cross Training, Rowing for Men & Women I've been using these for a few weeks and am happy with them. I measured my hand to be 8.5-8.75" and ordered XLarge based on the sizing chart. They are a good fit. Not great, but good. If anything, they might be a tad large, but that's mostly solved with the adjustable velcro strap.

The only serious drawback I've noticed is that when I bench-press, the left glove pinches my skin between my thumb and index finger. It's not so bad that I can't lift or I'd want to go back to lifting without the gloves. And, I don't get the pinching with other lifts. But, it's annoying and part of the reason I'm giving 4 stars.

Otherwise, I really like these gloves. I use them with free weights and feel that my grip is better and I can focus more on the strength exercise. Without gloves, I had to concentrate more on gripping the weight. And, my hands would hurt somewhat after lifting without the gloves. As others have noted, the padding is great for gripping unpadded rods and bar. All the weights I use are unpadded (just a textured metal rod) and I find the glove padding helpful. I wouldn't want to use these with a padded rod or bar as I think that they would not improve grip in that case.

text_fidelity_a:
Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Kuat Dirtbag

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker I'm a Fitbit lover. I track everything with it; steps, heart rate, activity, sleep, food, BMI, body fat. All these metrics warm my geeky little heart and help me achieve my health goals. I own a Flex, an Alta HR, and the Aria 2 scale and have adored all of them. Because I love them so much, I gave my husband a Charge 3 for his birthday. I'm sorry to say, this Fitbit product is a total dud. The tracker will not sync with Fitbit's app. It worked for about 1 month then just stopped syncing with the app. We've tried every flavor of delete-reinstall-reset possible, all to no avail. There are hundreds, maybe thousands, of people who have this same issue, who have reported it to Fitbit, and the response is unfortunately not in keeping with the company's usual excellent customer service. All they will offer people is another Charge 3. You can't even swap the tracker for a less expense, older model that works with their app. Without the app, without the ability to track and review a history, the Charge 3 is little better than the freebie plastic pedometers your employer's health insurance plan hands out at their annual Open Enrollment fair. What's more than a little irksome is that Fitbit seems unwilling to admit there's a major software problem here. Seems obvious when one reads the Help forums. Why not 'fess up and tell us an estimate of when we can expect a software update? I don't get it. People will likely be patient and wait for the update if they know one is in the works. What is to be gained by pretending nothing is wrong? A lot of very unhappy customers, that's what.

Long story short: Don't buy this tracker. Get a different one. Maybe even one not made by Fitbit (sorry, Fitbit!)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

If Lebron were coming over to jam, I would definitely want the extra build, but 4" is fine for me (used to be all you saw).

I don't adjust the height for anything else, but a younger version of myself would lower to allow for some likely sad looking jams.

The new redesigned camelbak valve on these is a huge improvement over the older ones, they seem to be more resistant to getting moldy in the first place.. and if they do it is quick and easy to disassemble for cleaning! Great job camelbak!

My only qualm with these bottles is that the plastic is very soft and gets marred/scratched very easily. This was kind of the case with the older camelbak bottles also but it seems even worse on these newer ones. It doesn't affect the function of the bottles so its not a huge issue but just kind of annoying that these look old and beat up after one or two rides whereas I have some other (non-camelbak) bottles that are several years old and still look practically new. That said, those other bottles use harder plastic which is more rigid and more difficult to squeeze, making them harder to drink from, and the ease of squeezing out a large amount of liquid is what makes the camelbak bottles so great, so its a tradeoff I'm willing to make..

I've noticed some reviewers complaining about them not fitting well in bottle cages but I've never had issues on any of my bikes, I use arundel cages on most of them but I have also have some specialized and lezyne cages.

Something to block the wind. A back-up warning light to protect you at night. No more forgetting your ride glasses or forgetting to charge your warning light and not having a backup...

PRO:
Great looking in pictures online. Great concept - eliminate a separate set of cycling glasses and also include a night time safety light. Good padding and adjustment strap. Extra safety light included!

CON:

Black Mountain Products Resistance Band Set with Door Anchor, Ankle Strap, Exercise Chart, and Carrying Case I bought this set of bands to work on rehabbing my knee outside of the gym. This type of product is certainly convenient to use and offers a fair amount of resistance for my purposes. However, for those intent on building gobs of muscle, weights are of course ideal. I found that I needed some time to adjust to the feel of these bands. While the manual indicates some type of pound rating it doesn't feel accurate. The nominal rating of weak to strong is a better way to judge the resistance of each band. I chose a familiar exercise that would allow me to work through a range of bands. I knew what I could lift with weights and compared that sensation to the band with a similar resistance. From there I could start to estimate which bands i might start with for other exercises. The kit is nicely put together with a wide range of bands and extra straps for doors and ankles. The carrying bag holds everything without being cramped and is well suited for travelling. As another reviewer noted, the bands are rubber and are subject to wear. It behooves the user to inspect them regularly before use.

Update: I have used this kit several times now and wanted to add a finding. I found the exercises more satisfying when contracting and holding the muscles being worked on at the end of the positive movement. This gives extra focus to the area at hand and makes the most out of the resistance that the bands offer. Hopefully, I am not overstating the obvious, but I found this feature easier to do with the bands than with free weights.

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software I have used a few different Omron pedometers in my day and like other consumers, I purchased this one due to the solid reviews. Anything with an overall rating as good as this product should be worth the money. So, with my old pedometer on the fritz, I decided it was time for a new one and purchased this model.

Omron Pocket Pedometer was okay at first. It does measure your total steps, aerobic steps, time, calories burned, and distance. The accuracy seems to be pretty good and I like that I can monitor my progress and check things online with the software. These are all good qualities and they earn the product some respectability.

Where this product loses some points with me is with its cumbersome display; its tendency to go blank; and the lack of any ability to shut it off. With the display, what I don’t like specifically is the annoyance with looking at your statistics from past days. It stores up to a week’s worth of data, which is great, but if you want to view the data from a past day, you have to toggle back and forth between two of the buttons. You can’t just simply go back to the day you want and then view the steps, aerobic steps, time, distance, and calories with one push. You have to push the button to the left a couple of times, then push the button on the right to view one stat, then push the button on the left a couple of times again to view the next stat, etc. Other pedometers are much easier than this.
Another problem is with the tendency of the screen to go blank. This happens to me anytime I drop the pedometer. I have to then get a small screwdriver to remove the back, move the battery around, and screw it back on. The display will them reappear. And, of course, there is the problem with inability to shut the pedometer off. With other pedometers, you can turn it off or it will shut off itself after a certain amount of time has elapsed. It doesn’t work that way here. The display is always on, draining the battery at a fast rate. Sure, you could pop out the battery after each use, but this is too much trouble. Just make sure you have plenty of replacement batteries on hand because you’re going to need them.

So, taken as a whole, this is device is not as good as I expected and I plan to search for a replacement very soon. It’s disappointing for something from Omron. I have had better luck with other pedometers from this company and cannot give this one a recommendation for the reasons cited.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software

RAYPOSE Womens Workout Capri Leggings for Women with Pockets Plus Size Capris Casual Summer Yoga Pants Women The Raypose High Waist Tummy Control Capri Yoga Pants have side mesh panels, pockets, and a unique fit. More about that later.

The material is dense, not see-through, and has a slight patina that is neither shiny or matte. I would call it more of a slight sheen.

The two mesh panels run the entire length of the outer legs and are only slightly see-through until you reach the pockets, which are lined, so your underwear will not be visible.

The pockets are only 3 1/2" wide and could not accommodate my XS Max, but may fit a smaller phone.

II received these leggings in size medium, but the fit is unlike any size medium I have tried before. I am 5'3", 116 lbs and wear a size small in bottoms, but I review size medium leggings all the time, and I am familiar with how it should fit my body.

When a size medium runs small, it will fit me at the crotch, and when it runs true to size, there is some bunching of excess fabric.

These do not even reach my crotch. I've never experienced that before. It reminded me of 60s style stretch pants with stirrups because the tight calves pulled the legs down and made them straight and taught. I was surprised by how snug the calves fit on my skinny legs.

I tried to pull them up as I high as possible to achieve a more comfortable fit, but the waistband reached to my bra line. Since I received them in a larger size, I rated these higher because I don't know if I would experience the same issues in the correct size, so I am giving them the benefit of doubt. Had these fit the same way in size small I would rate it at 3 stars.

I would recommend these for taller gals with long torsos and narrow calves.

text_fidelity_a:
Walker's Razor Slim The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would. I still would like to try those because it would be worth the money to me if they worked like they should but if they didn't I knew I would still be getting these.
text_fidelity_b: Walker's Razor Slim

BROTOU Sun Cap Fishing Hats, UPF 50+ Wide Brim Outdoor Protection Hat, Sun Hat with Face & Neck Flap Cover for Men and Women We love to hike in the mountains near our Colorado home, but unfortunately, high-altitude sun and bugs can make the aftermath very uncomfortable.

This hat has lots of protective options. First, there's a sturdy, multi-stitched extra-wide brim to shade your face. That alone will probably protect you from the sun (and rain).

If you hate hats because they make your head sweat, you won't mind wearing this one. The crown is lightweight, flexible, and vented. It also has a cord to adjust the size of the hatband! At first, I thought it was a bit big, but that was easy to fix. Hatmakers have finally realized that wind exists and are including chin cords. This model has a nice one. if those were the only features of this hat, it would probably would be enough, but wait, there's more.

My wife also wanted something she could set by the waterline and have the water on her feet and legs. So these short, low chairs were on our watch list. When I had the chance, I grabbed this HOMFUL Camping Beach Chair and so far, we’re glad I did. The bag comes in a nice bag, making for easy carrying. The chair sets up and comes apart really very easily - one person can easily do it - with the back/top of the back of the chair coming off the lower section, then folding or unfolding. Note the video above. The chair is very low to the ground - we have had one other set that actually was not as low and it was low. Getting in and out is like it is on any such chair. The arms are slanted, so rolling in or out is actually kind of easier than pushing up. They are also coated with a sort of rubber like material, making them softer to lay your arms on them. The cup holder is decent - it lays under the side, and I think it’ll hold many options - we only tired a water bottle. Funny thing - I think there is a small pouch under the front - but once you’re in it, you can’t see it and I forgot about it - couldn’t even feel it. So forgot it was even there. The chair comes with a nice little blow up pillow and pouch for it - bet you can stick it in that front pouch if you find it. It was easy to blow up by mouth and when my wife was seated, I had her try it - it works, seems nice - but no way to attach to the chair - which would have been a nice addition. It’s mid-winter so no chance to try it out - yet - but from what we are experiencing here in the house, it’s going to be a nice addition to our days at the beach - and we can’t wait. We so far like this HOMFUL Camping Beach Chair and happy to have it.

The Inspire 2 is a smaller display and, depending on the templates you download on the app, can have more details showing on the home screen. This is still a great buy if you only need the basics. All the features for heart rate, steps, and (this one shows) activity time are what you’re looking for when buying a watch like this.

Fitbit Charge 4 vs Inspire 2: What's the difference?
The Inspire 2 has a plastic body so it's a little cheaper in its appearance compared to the Charge 4. It also has a smaller touchscreen display than the Charge and it has a physical button on the side, making for a less streamlined design than the other two models.

Ultimately, it’s lightweight, compact, and doesn’t use up excessive power like other smartwatches on the market. It also charges pretty fast (20-30 minutes for a full charge) and it takes about 4-5 days to run out of power (2 days for smartwatches). I would definitely recommend that someone to buy it for fitness purposes.

Overall, an economical watch that does the job.

Cons: Fitbits stop working after a couple of years for no reason. This is my 4th one in the last 6 years.

text_fidelity_a:
Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz Pointing out a few things brought up in reviews:

1. This is DEHYDRATED zucchini, NOT freeze-dried. Very different methods, different results, different pricing. While Mother Earth does carry some freeze dried, they do not have freeze dried zucchini. Another way to tell? With freeze dried foods, they can be eaten as is (crunchy snack) or rehydrated. Where as with dehydrated foods, most all (except fruits, usually) will need to be rehydrated in order to consume them (too tough to eat). This will require soaking and/or cooking for a period of time. Can't just toss it in the dish you are making and expect it to cook up quickly. So for this, it says to simmer 1 part zucchini to 2 parts water for 10-30 minutes. This very well may take longer. I let it cook for no less than 30 minutes before adding it to what I ultimately want to have it be part of. Another way to get it started is to let soak, then follow up with a shorter simmer.

2. 1/2 cup dried zucchini = 1 cup cooked zucchini. I made up 1/4 cup and it made a very good sized portion. See my pics.

3. End result is NOT EVER going to be same as fresh. Stop that. Then stop blaming the company/brand. YOu will always be disappointed. Best thing to get if you cant get fresh or frozen is to find a company who makes freeze dried. Even then, you are expecting a lot from zucchini. This is similar to others, and there aren't many out there to choose from.

4. Shelf life can be very very long, if not indefinite if stored under proper conditions. Freeze dried for sure, but dehydrated can last a very long time. Be sure to keep it in well sealed container, out of light and dampness. Maybe keep in freezer or further repackaged into mylar or vac sealed jar.

5. Taste is neutral. Kind of like how zucchini can be. I could tell it was zucchini though! I found that with proper rehydration it worked well in adding bulk to tacos, and can always be added to soup. I see it as a nutritional item rather than a way to have a plate of zucchini. Nice way to bulk up meals, add vitamins and minerals, yet not have to rely on fresh (for various reasons). I noticed that the skins were more like late summer yellow squash/zucchini. Kinda reminded me of regular squash- like butternut skins. Not tough but had more "presence" I shall say. DID not taste or feel like "tree bark" in any way.

6. If planning on using it in zucchini bread, muffins, cookies, or sauces, I would recommend running it through the blender after it has been rehydrated. Make it more of a puree. This will impart flavor and decrease any tougher bits.

7. Says processed and packaged in USA, but WHERE do they get their vegetables from?? That I havent seen, here or on their web page

8. If you dont like this packaging, they also offer mylar bag style.

OVERALL: I think it is fine, and it as expected. I love seeing it in my pantry knowing that I have a variety of dehydrated foods to use when I cant get fresh, or food is scarce, or food doesnt look good, or I cant afford it that day. Buy a little here and there and stock up those cupboards. Would like to know where the zucchini comes from?

PS. I miss when we could comment and ask questions of other reviewers. One person just said "poisonous". Like, what do they even mean by that? I had this a few times and doing well so far :)
text_fidelity_b: Mother Earth Products Zucchini, Quart Jar, 8 oz

They took turns for the next hour or so. Before this, I had my son riding on a towel on my rear rack. He would hold my seat post and most of the time bury his face in my back so that he wouldn't fall off. He also had to hold his legs out so that his feet wouldn't get caught in the chain or the tire. With this seat, he can sit back in comfort, he has his own little handlebars to hold, and the seat is nice and soft for him. He is extremely happy that I got this for him.

Installation was a little difficult, but nothing crazy. I would have loved a second pair of hands to help me install, but the rest of my family was suddenly busy when I started putting it on. The only part that was hard was getting the crossbar on under the rack. One of the support beams would be right next to the bar, no matter how I installed the seat. It took a little maneuvering, but I managed to wedge the crossbar in and get the seat bolted down. Even if a nut falls off, I don't think the seat will move because of the way it is wedged on. So I feel it's very safe. One thing I wouldn't mind is having the brace that holds the backrest be a little more sturdy.

It's been a few weeks now and so far everything has held up. The bike was left out in the rain a few times, but I don't notice any rust appearing. I'm pretty pleased with this purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

text_fidelity_a: Meade 81015 Spotting Scope (Black) There are a number of things to consider when buying a spotting scope -- none of which I knew before buying this one.  One thing is MINIMUM focus.  For many this may not be an issue but for indoor target range shooting at 25 feet I cannot see 22 caliber hits in the bullseye and so I bought this.  Unfortunately the minimum focus distance is 28 feet.  Another factor is "eye relief" which is how close your eyeball needs to be to the focusing element -- in this case, very close -- which is an issue when I have my regular glasses plus safety glasses over them and as a result I cannot get close enough to the focusing element.  Some have criticized the tripod -- I agree that it is pretty cheap, especially when legs are extended.  However, for bench use without the legs extended the footprint is just 10x10x10 and height to the eyepiece is 20 inches.  It's plenty stable and just the right height.  As others have mentioned, the case is excellent.  After the little research I did, I ended up buying a Nikon Prostaff 5 at about $370.  Pricey compared to the Meade but far superior.  Focuses to 13 feet, has significant eye relief so I can use it without removing my glasses, and is much brighter.
text_fidelity_b: Meade 81015 Spotting Scope (Black)

G4Free 8pcs Lightweight Outdoor Camping Hiking Cookware Backpacking Cooking Picnic Bowl Pot Pan Set This is a wonderfully designed, compact set of camping cookware. Everything nests together perfectly—including the two plates, five bowls, bamboo stirrer and collapsible soup scoop, the pots with lids, and even a scrubber sponge!—and fits snugly in the included carrying bag. When I first pulled everything out, I tried the largest lid on the frying pan and it wasn't a tight fit. At first I thought that was a bad thing until I realized this is not a bulky set of kitchen pots and pans; the frying pan is just slightly larger than the largest pot so that the pot will nest into the frying pan to keep it all tidy and compact. The large lid, however, does cover the frying pan well enough to keep it from spattering.

At this price point, you couldn't ask for better materials. The only improvement that would be valuable to me is if the handles were coated with durable silicone instead of the red plastic. The plates are better quality melamine than the bowls, which are a thinner plastic, but they need to be thinner to fit so many into the kit.

The weight is a little less than 45 ounces, so it's not super lightweight, but for what's packed into this kit and the quality and versatility of the materials, I don't see how they could get it to weigh any less. We don't go camping much anymore, but what we will use this for is to keep at the ready along with an alcohol stove in case we have to be evacuated and wind up living out of our truck for a while! The kit will also be good to have on those few occasions when we have to cook for more than two people and need the extra pots and pans but don't have any place to store them in our small apartment. Because the handles fold against the sides of the pots, we could stick them into the fridge if there are leftovers until we can process or eat them.

Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike My wife had a gym membership that cost $60 a month. It was the best deal ever.........for the GYM! I've always been a workout at home guy. When our treadmill started failing after 15 years she cancelled her gym membership and we decided it was time to try something new. Due to hip issues (me) and knee issues (both of us) we needed something that would be comfortable, quiet, give the old heart a boost, and not aggravate our joint issues. The Exerpeutic 300SR exceeded our all our expectations.

My wife actually put the bike together when I was under the weather. The frame is strong and compact. The seat/backrest is comfortable. The mechanism is whisper quiet, quieter than any exercise bike we've ever used. Why lay on the couch watching TV when you can comfortably sit on the bike and do the same thing? The only weak part is the display. Hands off! It works absolutely fine but I can already see it breaking if someone tries to put their weight on it while getting on or off the bike. We've put a label on it that says "Not a handle - will break" to prevent occasional guests from making that mistake.

If the Exerpeutic 300SR lasts only three months, we're still ahead of what the gym membership cost. I suspect it will last much longer.

Update: 6 months and this baby gets a workout twice a day on most days, me in the morning and my wife in the evening. Still working perfectly!

text_fidelity_a:
Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick I’ve had my eye on another brand for awhile, but wasn’t sure - a single ring is around $25 - being concerned the silicone wouldn’t work, feel good, or have any give. My ring finger tapers and can go up and down during the day, so metal rings can go from loose to tight. Would this kind work? While not metal pricing, I still didn’t want to pay for another ring to sit in the drawer.

I am thrilled with these rings.

First, I got two sets: I literally fell on the line between the two sizes so figured it would be smarter than risking it. My ring finger is the smaller of the two, but I still get use of the larger set on other fingers. Usually not at the same time - looks a little goofy.

Second, I wasn’t sure on the grip - would they work on my tapered finger and would they have any give. Yes to both. In fact the only time I have an “issue” with being loose is washing my hands. I have to watch a bit, holding fingers tight, but otherwise the rings both stay snug and on, as well as give a little when humidity expands them. I love the fit, the size and look on my finger, and that little give.

Third, Yes, I keep them on when washing my hands, but I do take the ring off to dry it as well. Otherwise it will retain moisture - it does get annoying and loosens the fit. I have worn them to shower, but now keep it off, just in case.

Forth, working out and doing things with them on is a breeze. I lift weights (with/without gloves) play pickle ball, do chores, you name it, and the rings hold up. There is no issue and I don’t have to worry about damaging, bending, or otherwise having any problems.

Fifth, The Colors... Interesting. Some I love and look really nice on their own and on my hand. Some I just don’t like. It’s a personal taste thing, but some look cartoonish or goofy. Overall, it’s a personal thing, so have some fun. I was surprised I liked the look of the bright blue, red (thought I’d hate it), and tie dye.

Sixth, there is a slight difference between the cuts of these two sets I got. I include image to show: one is rounded, the other sharp cut. Not sure you can tell from product page the difference - I didn’t until they arrived.

These are some great rings for the price and I do like that I got different sizes. I do wear the larger ones on other fingers from time to time, but I love that I can now wear a wedding ring and not worry. (* Same review given for the other set in order to stay consistent with my experience)
text_fidelity_b: Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick
